name: Footprint names held modules
summary: Each changed module of a footprint names the changed modules bound inside it, so that the CLI gate and the pull-request Action judge a container the same way.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#mAh7CmuS
changes.value: A composite GitHub Action. It finds the proposal from its state input, the archboard-pr marker in the description, or the only draft. It reads the base and the head, and updates one sticky text comment on each push. The job needs only contents read and pull-requests write. The footprint compares the head with the base branch. With out-of-plan set to fail, a module changed outside the plan fails the job unless the override label is on the pull request. A changed module that holds another changed module is never outside the plan, as in the CLI gate. Below the footprint, the comment lists the changed files that no module is bound to, and never judges them.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/HBlhIeSD#radK8osF
changes.value: The history interface reads canonical states and their bound source declarations. Locality reports change frequency and coupling. Footprint compares explicit local refs and the selected proposal baseline, and lists each changed file that no binding holds, outside the vault. Each changed part names the other changed parts that its binding holds. Missing source stays unavailable rather than being replaced with current code.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/XppR9owz#MrE3v2T6
changes.value: The command passes explicit local source refs and selected architecture to the existing history interface. Proposal comparisons use their identified baseline. With --fail-outside and a draft, it exits 1 when the commits changed a module that the draft does not name, so a ticket merge without a pull request has a gate like the out-of-plan fail mode of the pull-request Action. A module bound to a directory, or to a .csproj project, fails the gate only when it holds no other changed module, because it changes with each of them. The footprint names those modules, and the Action applies the same rule. Without a draft it refuses the option. It names the changed files that no module is bound to, and they never fail the gate.
